title: The Front Desk Call
subtitle: Dial the number, and service swiftly follows. A good motel should offer nothing less.

items.text: Red Room, Tuesday's Motel
In the center of the red room stands a snow-white crib.
The hanging curtains sway slightly, like pulsating veins.
An arcanist with the head of a sheep stands there, silently observing the translucent fabric.
Footsteps draw closer, but she doesn't turn to face them.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Are you not satisfied with my services?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: No matter what, you shouldn't have cut the phone off.
The maid withdraws her hand from the telephone's hook switch with a hint of apology.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Nor should you have isolated me from the outside world.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Because you should know better than anyone what that means.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Why should I?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: All I know is that a poor, helpless child like you shouldn't be alone on the roadside.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Where's your mother? Didn't she tell you to be careful?
She sighs softly.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: You really don't remember anything, do you?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: What do you mean? What do you think I should remember?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Well, clearly, it doesn't matter now. This motel's well decorated. Did you do all this yourself?
The maid smiles.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Heh heh. Are all children like this? Always talking in circles to draw Mama's attention.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ah, but these innocent words make them all the more adorable.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I am not a child.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ha. That's exactly what a child would say.
She yields helplessly.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I've always felt a familiarity with you, like I've known you for a long time.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Can you tell me about it—why were you out here on Route 77 all alone?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Maybe I can help you.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Have you heard of UTTU?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, I have!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: It's a magazine about fashion, trends, and the avant-garde.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: My brother loved that magazine, but my father found it unacceptable—to think his eldest son would read those softies' magazines instead of working on the farm!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Fashion, trends, disco ... these aren't things a Texan man should pursue, at least according to my father.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: In the end, my father destroyed all my brother's disco records, along with his plane ticket to Los Angeles.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Perhaps that's for the best. He avoided the riots.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Nothing. So, what do you think?
She's treating the maid as an interview subject—the woman behind the legend, a chance not to be missed.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Me?
She looks somewhat surprised.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Why should I have any opinion?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Let me rephrase that. What impact has this had on you?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh.
Tuesday ponders for a moment, then shakes her head.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But what happened between them has nothing to do with me, does it?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: These were the choices they made.
She purses her lips, her face flushed.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: When I first arrived, a local resident told me not to stay at Tuesday's Motel.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: He said his aunt went mad soon after she stayed here.
The windows rattle gently, emitting a faint sound.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ha, I remember that lady. Her head was so large. It reminded me of those stories of people with deformities.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: So I had her "watch" a freak show at midnight. Sadly, she didn't seem to enjoy it.
A harvester starts up in the distance. The sound of the engine fills the room.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: At this time of year, the farmers run their combine harvesters on the fields nonstop. The harvest is a joyful time of year, but the accompanying noise always frightens the children.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Have you heard the stories? Of how naughty children get too close to harvesters and get caught in them, losing a hand or even a head, haha.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Fields, machinery, children with severed limbs ... Hmm, these stories are exactly what my motel's missing.
The window rattling grows more frantic.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, my baby's calling. Please excuse me; I don't want another temper tantrum on my hands.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Apologies, my fluffy little child. I look forward to our next conversation. Talking to you always brings me inspiration.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But the motel's been too busy lately. It's starting to get on my nerves.
The maid speaks slowly, her face flushed again.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: *cough*
Her cough is weak, like a sickly child's.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: See, this is what I mean. How could I bear to send you out on your own? You'll stay right here in this cozy little room until you're fully recovered.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I don't need this "special treatment" of yours. Staying here won't cure my illness.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Just get some sleep. You'll come to your senses after a good rest.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I'll see you soon.
The maid lightly steps out of the room.
Barbara watches as the door vanishes.
She looks at the pool of blood in the hallway where the officer's body once was.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: How many times have I told you not to eat things off the floor?
*cry*
The bundle in her arms suddenly lets out a strange cry.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: There, there. Don't cry, sweetheart.
